style: Realistic 35mm film photograph, heavy film grain, muted desaturated colors, faces hidden in shadow, Russia in the 1990s, Soviet-era interiors and courtyards, the logic of a dream, quiet, uneasy and unsettling atmosphere.

priorities.1: prototype gaps: locations without frames yet and scare frames
priorities.2: second frame for each location, more motifs

scenes.scene: An endless narrow corridor with pale green painted walls; hundreds of old glass mercury thermometers hang in neat rows on both walls like a museum display, all showing 37.2; dim yellow ceiling lamps fade into darkness at the far end

A long institutional corridor where a giant glass mercury thermometer, taller than a man, leans against the wall; far behind it a small figure in a bathrobe stands with its back to the camera under a flickering fluorescent tube

Underwater-like macro shot submerged inside thick dark red cherry jam, whole cherries and seeds suspended around the camera, everything glowing deep red and murky, the round mouth of the jar far above as a pale blurred circle of light, claustrophobic

A dacha cellar shelf crowded with old glass jars of home-made jam sealed with paper and string; one jar in the middle is enormous, as tall as a door, its lid ajar, a wooden ladder leaning against it; grey dusk light from a small window

A Soviet-era bedroom deep at night, only cold blue moonlight from the window, a patterned carpet hanging on the wall above an empty unmade bed, long shadows across the floor, the doorway to the dark corridor open, nobody in the room

A dark Soviet-era bedroom at night seen from the doorway, a sleeping figure in bed is only a dark silhouette under the blanket with the head turned to the wall, an old heart monitor on the bedside table glowing green is the only light, its glow on the wall and the pillow, the figure's face completely invisible in darkness

A cramped Soviet-era kitchen at night, the old white refrigerator door standing wide open, its pale yellow light the only light in the room, spilling over a linoleum floor and a small table with an oilcloth, dark window behind, nobody in the room

A kitchen table with an oilcloth in grey daylight, an open jar of cherry jam with a spoon standing upright in it, a glass mercury thermometer lying next to it, a glass of tea in a metal holder, a plain bare wall behind, nothing written anywhere

Inside a cramped old Soviet elevator cabin with brown wood-grain panels scratched with graffiti, a panel of burnt round buttons, one weak bulb behind a cracked plastic cover, the folding door half open onto blackness
A dim apartment block landing at night, metal elevator doors with a small round window glowing yellow; through the window a figure is visible standing motionless inside the cabin

An empty hospital corridor at night, a metal gurney with a white sheet standing alone in the middle of the corridor, an old heart monitor on a trolley beside it with a faint green line, flickering fluorescent tube overhead, pale tiled walls, doors closed, nobody in the corridor
A hospital ward seen through the glass of a door: an old ventilator with an accordion bellows next to a bed, a man lying under a sheet, his face in shadow, the monitor light reflecting on the glass
A pale human face suddenly very close to the camera in a dark stairwell, lit from below by a harsh flash, eyes wide and black, mouth slightly open, peeling green paint behind

A woman in a faded house dress standing right over the bed at night with an old Soviet vacuum cleaner hose raised, her face bent close to the camera, half lit by a harsh flash, eyes reflecting the light

A tall figure in a white hospital gown suddenly filling the frame in a dark hospital corridor, its face a smear of shadow and grey skin caught by a camera flash, the corridor behind it receding into black
Elevator doors open onto a cabin packed tightly with silent people in winter coats, all of them staring straight into the camera, faces grey in a harsh flash, no room to step in
A pale face pressed against the inside of a huge glass jar of dark red jam, eyes open, red syrup in the hair, a hand flat on the glass, lit by a harsh camera flash in a dark kitchen
A Soviet apartment courtyard at night in fog, a metal swing frozen high in mid-swing with nobody on it, a single sodium streetlight, rows of dark windows in a nine-storey panel block
Typewritten sheets of a last will scattered across the wet asphalt of a courtyard at dusk, stamped and signed, some stuck to a bench and a sandbox, panel apartment blocks behind in blue twilight
An overcast day in a courtyard between grey panel blocks, white sheets drying on ropes, a rusty climbing frame, a distant old woman on a bench with her back to the camera
Dozens of pigeons sitting motionless in rows on a snowy courtyard fence at night, all facing the same lit window on the ground floor, a streetlight humming above

A dark stairwell of a panel apartment block, a long vacuum cleaner hose snaking down the stairs from the floor above, at the top of the flight a woman's legs and the hem of a house dress under a bare bulb
A stairwell landing at night with a dirty window onto the courtyard, a radiator, cigarette butts in a tin can, peeling blue-green paint, the light on the floor below has gone out
Looking up the stairwell shaft of a Soviet apartment block, the railings spiralling upward far beyond the number of floors the building has, weak bulbs on each landing, the top lost in darkness
Concrete stairs of an apartment block with a mercury thermometer lying on every step, glinting under a single dim bulb, leading down to a closed basement door
Pigeons sitting on the steps of an indoor staircase at dusk, the stairwell window broken, feathers on the concrete, dusk light falling in blue stripes across the railings
A polyclinic corridor in grey daylight, a row of joined wooden chairs along the wall, one patient sitting at the far end with his head down, numbered white doors, a rubber plant in a pot
A nurse's desk in an empty hospital corridor at night, a typed last will lying under a desk lamp with a fountain pen on top, a rubber stamp, a ventilator hissing somewhere in the dark behind

A corridor floor covered with beads of spilled mercury from broken thermometers, reflecting the ceiling lamps like tiny mirrors, broken glass along the skirting board, a door at the end with a red lamp above it
A nurse in a white cap seen from behind at the far end of a corridor lined with thermometers in glass cases, she holds one up to the lamp to read it, her shadow stretched long across the linoleum
Extreme close-up of thick dark jam slowly dripping from a silver teaspoon into an open jar, a distorted reflection of a kitchen window in the jam surface, sticky glass rim
A bedside table at grey dawn: a thermometer in a plastic case, blister packs of pills, a glass of water, a wind-up alarm clock, a crumpled pillow beside it, net curtains lit pale blue

A hospital ventilator with an accordion bellows standing in an ordinary apartment bedroom at night, its tube running under the blanket of a sleeping figure, a wall carpet and a cassette radio on the shelf

A woman in a house dress vacuuming the floor of a dark Soviet kitchen at night with an old cylinder vacuum cleaner, seen from the hallway, her face turned away into shadow, a single bulb over the table
A dark kitchen at night where the glowing display of an old microwave oven shows a green heartbeat line instead of a clock, its light falling on a plate of cold food and a jar of jam
Close-up of an old elevator button panel with melted plastic buttons, the floors numbered up to 37, button 37 glowing faintly, scratched wood-grain walls, harsh flat light

A small bedroom in a Soviet apartment on a grey day, a patterned carpet hanging on the wall above an unmade bed, a wooden stool by the bed with a glass thermometer and a glass of tea, pale daylight through net curtains, nobody in the room

A huge black spider the size of a cat sitting in a thick dusty web in the upper corner of a Soviet apartment stairwell, peeling green paint, a single dim bulb below, concrete steps leading up into darkness, nobody there

A dark Soviet-era bedroom at night seen from the bed, an enormous spider as big as a dog clinging to the ceiling right above the bed, its long legs spread across the cracked plaster, faint streetlight through the curtains, nobody else in the room

A long empty hospital corridor at night, a long dark snake slowly crawling across the worn linoleum floor in the middle of the corridor, flickering fluorescent tubes, pale tiled walls, closed doors, nobody there
A cramped Soviet-era kitchen at night lit only by a weak bulb, a thick snake coiled inside the old enamel sink among unwashed dishes, its head raised over the edge, a dripping tap, nobody in the room

An empty Soviet courtyard at dusk, an old metal swing hanging still, a long snake wrapped around one of the swing chains and hanging down towards the seat, grey panel apartment blocks behind, bare trees, nobody there
Extreme close-up of a giant hairy spider lunging straight at the camera in a pitch-dark room, its many glossy black eyes reflecting a harsh camera flash, fangs open, legs filling the whole frame
Extreme close-up of a large snake striking straight at the camera out of darkness at the edge of a bed, mouth wide open, fangs bared, lit by a harsh camera flash, the pillow blurred behind it

A small Soviet-era bedroom at night almost completely filled by three enormous smooth grey spheres, each three times taller than a man, pressing against the walls and the ceiling, a man in pajamas standing tiny beside them with his face in shadow, a weak lamp

Three gigantic plain grey concrete cubes, each as tall as a three-storey building, standing in the middle of an empty Soviet courtyard at dusk, one cube tilted and balanced on its edge, a tiny man far below them in the foreground looking up, grey panel apartment blocks around
A narrow Soviet apartment stairwell completely blocked by one gigantic smooth white ball wedged between the walls and the steps, far too big for the space, peeling paint, a dim bulb, nobody there
